messages:
elaine: heads up — vendor dropped a new model bundle (ClipperX v2.3) into /mnt/models/clipperx-2.3.tar.gz. I started a quick perf eval but legal flagged some packaging notes. can @sam-legal weigh in?
ryan: saw that. quick context: we want to onboard it to hosted catalog and run quantization/latency bench. need to confirm rehosting + commercial use ok.
sam-legal: thanks, looping in. do we have the upstream license text?
elaine: uploaded snippet from METADATA.txt: ```License: Custom-ML-NonTransfer v1.0
You may use the model weights for internal inference and host via a service you operate. Redistribution of model weights or derivative model files (including quantized binaries) to third parties is prohibited. Attribution required: include "ClipperX by AcmeAI" in product docs.```
sam-legal: OK three quick flags: (1) "prohibited redistribution" = we can't ship the quantized weights as part of any customer-facing downloadable package or expose a direct weight-download endpoint. (2) "host via a service you operate" suggests hosting in our hosted API is OK, but private deployment (customer-managed) could be gray if we transfer weights to customer infra. (3) attribution clause is fine but make sure UI copy is non-misleading.
tom: about (2) — Dedicated customers often want a container with weights. if license prohibits redistribution we might need a managed-delivery-only approach (we keep weights in our infra and provide inference proxy).
ryan: for quantization experiments: can we keep quantized artifacts ephemeral on our infra for caching/serving? license says "derivative model files (including quantized binaries)" prohibited for redistribution, but doesn't forbid ephemeral derived files used internally. how strict is that? @sam-legal
sam-legal: ephemeral internal derivatives for serving should be OK, assuming they never leave our controlled storage or get packaged for customer download. we should record that in the onboarding note and add a delivery restriction checkbox. also need to capture vendor contact and any commercial carveouts.
elaine: action items: 1) block weight-download endpoints for ClipperX in hosted catalog, 2) update onboarding doc with "no-redistribute" tag and delivery constraints, 3) log vendor contact + license text. I'll also add a runtime flag to avoid persisting quantized artifacts to the public AMI.
license-bot: license-scan complete for ClipperX v2.3 — FLAG: custom-nontransfer detected, attribution required. See /legal/scan/1745678901-report.txt
ryan: one more: we do benchmarking against other models; can we publish aggregate numbers? no proprietary weight redistribution there but what about publishing accuracy numbers with model name? vendor requires attribution but not data suppression. @sam-legal thoughts?
sam-legal: publishing eval results + model name is OK under current text, just include required attribution. avoid publishing or sharing the weights or any reproducible build instructions that would enable reconstruction from our quantized blobs.
tom: noted. I'll change bench runner to redact any artifact links and add a note in results dashboard that weights are not downloadable.
elaine: thanks all. i'll open a short onboarding checklist PR with the restrictions and tag infra for the ephemeral quant cache change.
ryan: thanks — I'll hold any customer demo that copies weights out. :thumbsup:
sam-legal: happy to review the PR. also request to add a vendor contact field in model metadata for future legal follow-ups.
elaine: will do. closing thread once PR is up.
